title: Beef Empanadas
subtitle: Argentinian hand pies with spiced beef filling
excerpt: Empanadas are pastry parcels stuffed with a well-seasoned beef filling. This Argentinian-style version includes black olives and smoky paprika for depth. They work as a starter, a snack, or a main with salad.
sourceNotes: Based on Argentinian empanada tradition. Fillings vary by region; this version draws from the northern style with olives and spice.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncooked empanadas on a tray, then bag them. Bake from frozen at 200C for 30 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch easily. The filling keeps for 2 days in the fridge.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make and fill the empanadas a day ahead. Refrigerate on a lined tray and bake to order.

content.text: Make the filling first and let it cool completely before assembling. A hot filling will make the pastry greasy and hard to seal.

items.prepNote: 1 for dough, 1 beaten for egg wash

content.text: Make the pastry. Pulse flour and butter in a food processor until breadcrumb-like. Add 1 egg and 4 tbsp cold water. Pulse until the dough just comes together.
Shape into a disc. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Make the filling. Cook onion and pepper in a dry pan over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add garlic, cumin, paprika, and chilli flakes. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the beef mince. Break it up and cook until browned, about 8 minutes. Stir in the olives. Season well. Leave to cool completely.
Heat the oven to 200C. Line the baking tray with baking paper.
Roll the dough to 3mm thick. Cut out 12 circles about 14cm across.
Place 2 tbsp of filling in the centre of each circle. Fold in half. Press the edges firmly, then crimp with a fork to seal.
Brush with beaten egg. Bake for 20 to 22 minutes until golden.

items.cause: Edges not sealed properly, or filling was too wet
items.fix: Press edges firmly and crimp tight. Drain any excess fat from filling.
Mix until just combined and chill for the full 30 minutes.
Brown the mince only until it loses its pink colour.
